builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Dual-Axis Policy Optimization for LLM Agents: Bayesian Feedback Attribution and Trajectory Mass Normalization
summary: It replaces the credit-assignment and batch-aggregation components of standard GRPO/GiGPO with Bayesian feedback attribution within trajectories and equal-mass normalization across trajectories, leaving the underlying RL loop and base model unchanged. The cost is additional inference-time posterior computation per step, rollout collection for RL, and extra hyperparameters, all within a training workflow that still demands substantial sampling. Failure modes include mis-specified feedback posteriors in environments with sparse or noisy rewards, instability from equalizing trajectory mass when task difficulty is highly heterogeneous, and the possibility that gains measured on small agentic benchmarks do not transfer to production task distributions.
rationale: The method is implemented as modifications to existing GRPO/GiGPO training and could be run at small scale with LoRA on modest models, but the claimed gains are unquantified and RL fine-tuning with environment rollouts is compute-intensive enough that workload-specific validation is required before production adoption.
technique: Dual-axis RL policy optimization for LLM agents

claims.statement: It replaces the credit-assignment and batch-aggregation components of standard GRPO/GiGPO with Bayesian feedback attribution within trajectories and equal-mass normalization across trajectories, leaving the underlying RL loop and base model unchanged. The cost is additional inference-time posterior computation per step, rollout collection for RL, and extra hyperparameters, all within a training workflow that still demands substantial sampling. Failure modes include mis-specified feedback posteriors in environments with sparse or noisy rewards, instability from equalizing trajectory mass when task difficulty is highly heterogeneous, and the possibility that gains measured on small agentic benchmarks do not transfer to production task distributions.

Both axes provide independent gains and their combination achieves the strongest overall performance across model scales on ALFWorld, WebShop, and SearchQA; no absolute or multiplicative figures are stated in the abstract.
